list.snippet: Rest: Getting plenty of rest is crucial for recovery.
Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids like water, broth, or electrolyte drinks to stay hydrated, according to Baylor Scott & White Health.
Symptom Relief: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) can help with fever and pain. Cough syrups or lozenges can also provide relief.
Isolate: Stay home and away from others to prevent spread, especially if your symptoms are worsening, according to Mayo Clinic.
Track Symptoms: Keep a record of your symptoms and how they change over time.

related_questions.question: What are the best things to do when you have COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: When dealing with COVID-19, focus on symptom management and preventing further spread. Rest, stay hydrated, and consider over-the-counter medications for symptom relief. Isolate yourself to protect others, and practice good hygiene. If you have risk factors or severe symptoms, seek medical advice promptly, especially as treatment needs to begin within 5-7 days of symptom onset.
snippet_highlighted_words: Rest, stay hydrated, and consider over-the-counter medications for symptom relief

list.snippet: Rest: Allow your body to recover by getting plenty of sleep.
Hydration: Drink lots of fluids to prevent dehydration.
Over-the-counter medications: Consider pain relievers and fever reducers like acetaminophen or ibuprofen, and cough suppressants if needed, according to the CDC.
Monitor symptoms: Keep track of your symptoms and note any changes, especially if you experience shortness of breath or chest pain.
Isolation: Stay home and away from others to prevent transmitting the virus.
Hygiene: Wash your hands frequently and thoroughly with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, says the Mayo Clinic.
Cover coughs and sneezes: Use a tissue or your elbow to cover your mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, and discard used tissues immediately.
Disinfect surfaces: Clean and disinfect frequently touched surfaces like doorknobs, light switches, and countertops.
Consider a separate bathroom and bedroom: If possible, use a separate bathroom and bedroom to minimize contact with others in your household.
Ventilation: Improve airflow in your home by opening windows and using fans.
